page.layout: One page of title text at full width at the top, with a folding map engraving below it. No columns, no margin notes. Page number at top left.; Top: a folded map plate with the caption "CAP. I." below it at full width; then a heading in italic; then a large decorated initial with the text beside it in one main column; a narrow marginal note column at the left with notes beside the first lines; a line number "10" at the right beside the text; the verse lines centred; a catchword "Sub" at the lower right.

main_text.l: ERRAM Adjunctorum respectu distribui, flagitat ordo,
ut quo modo Partium ratione dividatur, aperiam. Ter-
rarum Orbem Veteres, quibus non ita, ut nobis hodie,
innotuerat, nunc in Duas Partes, nunc in Tres sunt par-
titi: Qui in Duas, Asiam & Europam, alios Africam
comprehendisse lego sub Asia, alios sub Europa. Sub Asia
de quo M. Terentius Varro lib. 1. de Re Rustica,
cap. 11; Primum quum Orbis Terra divisus sit in duas Partes ab
Eratosthene, maxime secundum naturam, ad Meridiem versus, & 10

l.i: & ad Septemtriones; Et sine dubio, quoniam salubrior pars Septemtrionalis est quam Meridiana, & quae
salubrior, illa fructuosior; dicendum magis Europam fuisse oportunam ad colendum, quam Asiam,
ibique Italiam; primum, quod est in Europa, secundo, quod haec temperatior pars est, quam interior;
nam intus pene sempiternae hiemes: & ipse Varro lib. 1. de Lingua Latina: Ut omnis,
inquit, natura in Caelum & Terram divisa est: sic Caelum in Regiones, Terra in Asiam & Europam. Asia enim

main_text.l: iacet ad Meridiem & Eurum; Europa ad Septemtriones & Aquilonem. Respicit
eo Silius Italicus lib. 1. Belli Poenici:

l.i: Aut ingens Asiae latus, aut pars Tertia Rerum.

marginalia.note: Orbis Terra-rum Duas Partes, Asiam & Europam faciunt Ve-teres;

page.notes: An engraved map of Europe begins below the title and runs off the bottom of this part. Its labels include Americæ Pars, Groenlandiæ Pars, Oceanus, Tartariæ Pars, Asiæ, Islandia, Hyperboreus Oceanus and Deucaledonius. The labels are too small and blurred to transcribe reliably, so they are not given here. The map plate above the text is not transcribed. The marginal note column on the left is copied. The line number 10 stands at the right of the text.
